rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the new modules each hide substantial behaviour behind a stated small surface: the EDDB extractor is one batch-fetch function plus one cache writer, the SELENE converter one entry point, the tokamap exporter one public function, and the §4 store-layout change is a single widened protocol method carrying catalogue-driven addressing.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the recurring duplicates are routed through their owners: mirror/cache paths through `imas_ambix/data/paths.py` (`JT60SA_ROOT` beside `MIRROR_ROOT`), description geometry through `gs/artifact_resolution.resolve_machine_description`, shot identity through `spine_bench/shots.py`, and probe-angle supply through `read_geometry_table`; the plan names `manifest.py`/`cli.py` and the MAST-only `gs/geometry.py load_tables` and the benchmark `transform_geometry_source` explicitly as owners it does not fork.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the plan adds no CLI or MCP surface by design ("adds no `ambix data` command"), and every section that adds a public definition accounts for it in its own text — §2 exporter ("retires nothing, because ambix has no exporter"), §3 extractor ("retires nothing, because ambix has no remote reader today"), §4 converter and widened `StoreEngine.open` and catalogue keys (each stating what it retires or that no slot existed), §7 EQDB reader and record fields (each stating retirement or why none).
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searches both named repositories and cites the existing mechanism for every subsystem it extends (`load_packaged_signal_map`, `read_geometry_table`, `cocos_convention`, `efit_referee`, `artifact_resolution`, `spine_bench/shots.py`, `load_machine_map`); each was opened and matches the plan's account, and no JT-60SA map or JT-60SA reader pre-exists in ambix.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every layer the plan adds is a new capability with a stated reason not to extend an existing one: §3 declines to import imas-codex's remote layer (dependency isolation) and states when a shared core would become cheaper; §4 declines a second deck store engine and extends `NetCDFTransformEngine.open` instead; §7 routes the EQDB reader through the §3 transport rather than a second path.
